video.title: So - how does the Internet really work
video.speaker: Johanna

queries.text: Where does she explain what she wants beginners to take away from the talk?
queries.evidence_description: The speaker lists understanding core concepts, losing fear of networks, experimenting, and debugging as her goals.
queries.why_interval_answers: The goals are stated continuously in speech; the slide alone only gives short headings.

queries.text: Find the part where she describes what a browser receives to display a website.
queries.evidence_description: She explains that HTML source describes text, appearance, and downloaded images.
queries.why_interval_answers: The spoken explanation directly answers what is transferred to the browser.

queries.text: When does she explain why Internet data is split into packets?
queries.evidence_description: The postcard analogy leads to the roughly 1,500-byte message size and packet splitting.
queries.why_interval_answers: The interval contains the complete spoken reason and packet terminology.

queries.text: Find the explanation of how a network switch learns where devices are.
queries.evidence_description: Alice, Blair, and the teacher illustrate flooding an unknown destination and learning a sender's tube.
queries.why_interval_answers: The speaker explicitly maps the classroom behavior to a home-network switch.

queries.text: Where does she say wired Ethernet and Wi-Fi work similarly for this explanation?
queries.evidence_description: Ethernet and Wi-Fi are described as members of IEEE 802 and functionally equivalent at this abstraction.
queries.why_interval_answers: The equivalence is a spoken qualification rather than merely a visual comparison.

queries.text: When does she explain why MAC addresses need to be globally unique?
queries.evidence_description: She explains that each interface has a burned-in address and computers cannot handle ambiguous names well.
queries.why_interval_answers: The interval states both uniqueness and its practical reason.

queries.text: How does she suggest choosing the right interface in Wireshark?
queries.evidence_description: She recommends selecting the interface whose squiggly activity graph shows the most traffic.
queries.why_interval_answers: The recommendation and its rationale are both spoken here.

queries.text: Find where she explains why a device needs a lower-level address before it can get an IP address.
queries.evidence_description: A new device first identifies itself with its burned-in name so the IP assignment can be returned.
queries.why_interval_answers: The speech explicitly connects Ethernet identity to obtaining an IP address.

queries.text: Where does she explain how pinging 9.9.9.9 can help diagnose a DNS problem?
queries.evidence_description: She describes ping, pong replies, and using 9.9.9.9 to distinguish DNS failure from lower-level connectivity failure.
queries.why_interval_answers: This interval contains the complete troubleshooting logic.

queries.text: What tools does she recommend for experimenting with networks after the talk?
queries.evidence_description: She recommends GNS3, Containerlab, Raspberry Pi BGP practice, Wireshark, Linux services, and distributed lab networks.
queries.why_interval_answers: The closing advice names the practical tools and ways to experiment.

queries.text: Show me the slide with three orange goal bars.
queries.evidence_description: A white Goals slide contains three horizontal orange gradient bars.
queries.why_interval_answers: The requested layout is clearly visible throughout the interval.

queries.text: Find the browser page followed by its HTML source code.
queries.evidence_description: The projected content changes from the EMF website in a browser to a page of HTML source.
queries.why_interval_answers: Both requested visual states appear consecutively and are legible as browser/source views.

queries.text: Show the hand-drawn postcards used in the networking analogy.
queries.evidence_description: Two and later three handwritten postcard rectangles show short From and To messages.
queries.why_interval_answers: The postcards are the dominant slide graphic.

queries.text: Find the slide showing three different home networking boxes.
queries.evidence_description: Three product photos show black, white-red, and upright white home network devices.
queries.why_interval_answers: All three boxes are simultaneously visible on the slide.

queries.text: Show the old black-and-white picture of pneumatic tubes.
queries.evidence_description: A monochrome archival photograph of a bank of pneumatic tubes appears beside text.
queries.why_interval_answers: The distinctive photograph is visibly present in this short interval.

queries.text: Find the diagram with Alice and Blair sending messages through a teacher.
queries.evidence_description: Named person icons for Alice and Blair connect by animated arrows to a teacher icon.
queries.why_interval_answers: The named diagram and message arrows are clearly visible.

queries.text: Show the IEEE 802 slide comparing a round Wi-Fi access point with an Ethernet switch.
queries.evidence_description: The IEEE 802 slide places a circular Wi-Fi device on the left and a black Ethernet switch on the right.
queries.why_interval_answers: The two device images and labels are visible together.

queries.text: Find the Wireshark packet window with yellow circles around address fields.
queries.evidence_description: A Wireshark packet-detail window shows yellow oval annotations around source and destination address rows.
queries.why_interval_answers: The requested application view and annotations are visibly present.

queries.text: Show the network switch while she explains that it learns connected devices from their first messages.
queries.evidence_description: The explanation concludes over the learned-path diagram and transitions to a photographed network switch.
queries.why_interval_answers: Speech supplies the learning behavior while the visual identifies the physical switch.

queries.text: Find the IPv4 and IPv6 examples while she says the longer one only looks more intimidating.
queries.evidence_description: The IP Addresses slide shows 192.168.0.1 and a long IPv6 address as she compares them.
queries.why_interval_answers: The wording refers to the spoken judgment and the two visible address forms.

queries.text: Show the green network part and yellow host part while she explains an IPv4 address.
queries.evidence_description: An IPv4 address is highlighted green for Network and yellow for Host during the verbal decomposition.
queries.why_interval_answers: The color-coded visual and spoken meaning are both required.

queries.text: Find the colored nested message diagram while she explains Ethernet, IP, and the payload as layers.
queries.evidence_description: Green Ethernet, yellow IP, and blue payload rows build up beside the network diagram.
queries.why_interval_answers: The colors identify visible layers while speech explains their nesting and roles.

queries.text: Show the home router's yellow and blue ports while she explains which side is LAN and WAN.
queries.evidence_description: A home router rear panel shows grouped yellow and blue ports as the speaker distinguishes local and wide area sides.
queries.why_interval_answers: The query requires the visible port colors and the spoken LAN/WAN explanation.

queries.text: Find the DHCP diagram when a new device asks what its IP address should be.
queries.evidence_description: The DHCP slide animates a handwritten IP question and assignment between Alice and the gateway.
queries.why_interval_answers: The visible exchange and spoken address-assignment sequence jointly answer the query.

queries.text: Show the DNS request moving through the network while she explains how a domain becomes an IP address.
queries.evidence_description: Blue and red arrows connect clients, a gateway, the Internet cloud, and a DNS server while lookup steps are narrated.
queries.why_interval_answers: The animation shows the path while speech supplies the domain-to-address meaning.

queries.text: Find the network-cloud diagram while she explains how BGP chooses a shorter route between autonomous systems.
queries.evidence_description: Several AS clouds and router icons receive blue and red path arrows as BGP announcements and route choice are explained.
queries.why_interval_answers: The route alternatives are visual, while BGP and shortest-path meaning come from speech.

queries.text: When does she compare TCP with UDP?
queries.evidence_description: The full transcript contains no TCP-versus-UDP comparison.
queries.why_interval_answers: Verified absent by full transcript and frame review before search.

queries.text: Show me the world map of undersea Internet cables.
queries.evidence_description: No world map or undersea-cable visualization appears in the reviewed frames.
queries.why_interval_answers: Verified absent across all 366 review frames before search.

queries.text: Find the phone screen while she explains mobile data.
queries.evidence_description: The talk mentions browsers on phones briefly but shows no phone screen and gives no mobile-data explanation.
queries.why_interval_answers: The required combined evidence is absent from the full frame and transcript review.

queries.text: Show the slide with a padlock icon for HTTPS encryption.
queries.evidence_description: HTTPS and TLS are spoken, but no padlock icon appears on any slide.
queries.why_interval_answers: The specific requested visual evidence is absent despite related speech.
